summary: Master permanganometry, dichrometry, direct iodimetry, indirect iodometry, and sodium thiosulfate mechanics.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
REDOX TITRATION TYPES
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                                 ▼                                 ▼
PERMANGANOMETRY                  DICHROMETRY                      IODOMETRY / IODIMETRY
├── KMnO₄ in Acidic Medium       ├── K₂Cr₂O₇ in Acidic            ├── Iodimetry: Direct I₂ titration
├── Self-Indicator               ├── Requires Diphenylamine       └── Iodometry: Indirect I₂ release
└── Purple → Colorless (Mn²⁺)    └── Orange → Green (Cr³⁺)            via Hypo (Na₂S₂O₃) + Starch
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Permanganometry**:
   - Titrant: $\text{KMnO}_4$ in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ medium.
   - **Self-Indicator**: Deep purple $\text{MnO}_4^-$ acts as its own indicator, discharging to colorless $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ until a faint pink persistence marks the end point.
2. **Dichrometry**:
   - Titrant: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ medium.
   - Requires an **Internal Redox Indicator** (Diphenylamine) because orange $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ reduces to green $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, obscuring visual end points. Excess oxidant oxidizes diphenylamine to deep blue-violet diphenylbenzidine.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Iodimetry vs. Iodometry and Hypo Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Iodimetry vs. Iodometry and Hypo Mechanics
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
IODIMETRY vs IODOMETRY SCHEMATIC
                       
IODIMETRY (Direct Titration):
Reducing Agent + Standard I₂ Solution ──[Starch]──► 2I⁻ (End point: Deep Blue appears)
   
IODOMETRY (Indirect Titration):
Step 1: Oxidant (Cu²⁺, Cr₂O₇²⁻) + Excess KI ──► Liberated I₂
Step 2: Liberated I₂ + 2Na₂S₂O₃ ──[Starch]──► 2NaI + Na₂S₄O₆ (End point: Blue disappears)

Hypo Reaction: I₂ + 2S₂O₃²⁻ → 2I⁻ + S₄O₆²⁻  ⟹  n-factor of Hypo = 1 (E.M. = Molar Mass)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Iodimetry (Direct Titration)**: Reducing agents are titrated directly with standard $\text{I}_2$ in the presence of starch. End point: **Deep blue color appears**.
• **Iodometry (Indirect Titration)**: An oxidizing agent ($\text{Cu}^{2+}, \text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$) reacts with excess $\text{KI}$ to liberate free $\text{I}_2$. The liberated $\text{I}_2$ is titrated against standard Sodium Thiosulfate (Hypo, $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$). End point: **Deep blue starch-iodine color DISAPPEARS** (becomes colorless).
• **n-Factor of Hypo**:
  $$\text{I}_2^{(0)} + 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2- (+2)} \rightarrow 2\text{I}^{- (-1)} + \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2- (+2.5)}$$
  $$n\text{-factor of } \text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 = 2 \times |2.5 - 2.0| = \mathbf{1} \implies \mathbf{\text{E.M.} = \text{Molar Mass}}$$

quickRevision: KMnO₄ is a self-indicator (purple to colorless/faint pink).
K₂Cr₂O₇ requires diphenylamine indicator (turns deep blue-violet).
Iodometry: indirect titration against Hypo (blue disappears).
n-Factor of Hypo (Na₂S₂O₃) in iodometry is 1 (E.M. = Molar Mass).
